pages.h2: Which version of the Buurtzorg story are you repeating?
pages.label: Read the myth check

post:
Buurtzorg, the Dutch home-care provider run by self-managing nurse teams, is cited worldwide as proof that autonomy cuts costs. We traced one version of that claim, relayed by a 2015 Commonwealth Fund case study, back to Dutch government documents.

The primary source is a KPMG Plexus study that state secretary Van Rijn sent to Parliament in January 2015. It compared Buurtzorg with about 600 home-care providers on 2013 claims data.

The hours part of the claim holds: 108 hours of home care per client per year, against 168 on average. The cost part needs a correction. Buurtzorg's hourly rate and its follow-on costs for GPs and hospitals were higher, and once every cost is counted, it came out about €500 cheaper per client, roughly 3% of total cost.

Our verdict: the claim partly holds.

Link to the full myth check in the comments.
short: Does Buurtzorg cost less? Dutch government figures: 108 care hours per client against 168, but a total cost only about 3% below average. The claim partly holds.
